subject: Follow-up: Isolation requirements & deployment mode evaluation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@fintrust.com>, Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Isolation requirements & deployment mode evaluation

Hi Sofia / Alex,

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the clarity on FinTrust's high-volume document-summarization pilot and the data residency constraints. Below is a short recap from our call and a couple of targeted questions so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Recap (what I heard)
- Use case: batch and near-real-time ingestion of customer documents (PII present) for summarization and semantic search.
- Volume: peak ~600 concurrent requests, steady-state ~120 req/s; tokens-heavy prompts with 8k average output windows.
- Primary requirement: logical and contractual isolation of customer data; some datasets are classified as regulated (financial records).
- Secondary: want predictable latency for their customer-facing product.

Open questions (so we scope correctly)
1) Isolation level required: physical separation (single-tenant GPUs / no shared kernel-level resources) vs strong logical isolation (VPC peering with dedicated tenancy and strict RBAC)?
2) Key custody preference: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in their cloud account, or Redwood-managed keys but with strict audit and export controls?
3) Audit evidence: what artifacts would you need to sign off (SOC2 + config screenshots, KMS proof, network diagrams, access logs retention window)?

Next steps I propose
- If you prefer physical single-tenant isolation and KMS in your account: we should evaluate Private VPC or on-prem deployment. That will trigger our security package and an infra feasibility review.
- If logical isolation (strong VPC boundaries + dedicated pools) is sufficient: Dedicated capacity with VPC endpoints is likely the faster path.

I attached a short comparison doc that highlights tradeoffs and typical timelines. Can you confirm the answers to the three questions above, and whether you want Diego (solutions engineer) to run a tech deep-dive next week?

Thanks — I’ll stand by for your preference and will schedule the SOC / infra review accordingly.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-vpc-compare-20260822.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@fintrust.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@fintrust.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Isolation requirements & deployment mode evaluation

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below.

1) Isolation level: we need single-tenant logical isolation at a minimum (no data commingling at the application or storage layer). Physical single-tenant GPUs would be preferred for the regulated data buckets, but not strictly required if we get explicit guarantees and attestations.
2) Keys: customer-managed KMS in our AWS account for the regulated buckets.
3) Audit evidence: SOC 2 report, diagram showing data flow and where keys are managed, encryption-in-transit/out-at-rest confirmation, retention and deletion workflows + sample logs for access.

Two other constraints:
- We must ensure that debug / tracing logs never carry PII values.
- The legal team wants a proposed timeline for a Private VPC evaluation (how long to stand up, required change window, and whether there is an outage risk).

We'd like Diego to run the tech deep-dive and see an initial checklist for Private VPC. If the deep-dive shows low blocker risk, we can run a dedicated-pool pilot in parallel.

- Sofia
Director, Cloud Engineering
FinTrust Financial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@fintrust.com>, Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Isolation requirements & deployment mode evaluation

Sofia — appreciate the quick clarity. Adding a few operational details so expectations are explicit, and looping in Monica from our security team to own evidence collection.

Operational clarifications
- \"Single-tenant logical isolation\" (what we call Dedicated capacity) provides tenant-level compute and storage separation: no shared application-layer tenants, dedicated GPU pools, and isolated model serving instances. It is not the same as an air-gapped on-prem install.
- Private VPC (customer-managed VPC) gives you the highest level of control: we run control-plane components in our managed environment but data plane lives in your VPC unless you opt for a fully on-prem package. That enables customer KMS and private peering.
- For regulated buckets, customers commonly combine Private VPC + customer KMS. Timeline notes below.

Timeline (ballpark)
- Dedicated pilot (Redwood-managed): 2–3 weeks to provision and validate; minimal infra work on your side.
- Private VPC discovery + feasibility: 1–2 weeks; provisioning and secure peering typically 3–6 weeks depending on change window and VPN/DirectConnect approvals.

Monica — can you prepare a checklist for the evidence Sofia requested (SOC2 excerpt, network diagram, KMS flow, example audit logs with data redaction), and list any open technical gating items we should highlight in the deep-dive?

Next actions for FinTrust
1) Confirm willingness to provision AWS cross-account roles for our infra automation during Private VPC setup (we can limit scopes).
2) Confirm available time for a 60–90m technical deep-dive next week with Diego + Monica.

I'll hold off on starting any provisioning until we have the deep-dive date.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia / Alex — Diego here, thanks for the context. I can run the technical deep-dive Thursday 2026-08-26 at 10:00 AM PT unless another time works better. Agenda I propose:

1) Deep-dive on data flow (ingest -> storage -> inference -> logs) with network diagrams.
2) Clarify what we persist and for how long; walk through our redaction/PII handling hooks.
3) KMS options: cross-account CMKs and HSM assurance, plus sample key rotation flows.
4) Deployment options: live demo of Dedicated pool provisioning; overview of Private VPC connector and required cross-account roles.
5) Evidence & deliverables checklist (Marissa / Monica to present).

Prep requests from FinTrust (please, before the call)
- Sample data classification matrix (you mentioned you have one) — that will help us map which buckets need Private VPC vs Dedicated.
- Contact for your infra team to coordinate cross-account role setup.

I will attach a short checklist doc and the standard Private VPC runbook after the call. If the time above works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include dial-in + Zoom.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
